findings.title: Graph extraction is the hard part and is specified as "grep for the needed section"
findings.description:
"Read discipline" says to grep `knowledge-graph.json` and never load it whole, but the file is JSON, not line-oriented text.
- **Minified output:** if the plugin writes one line, a grep returns the entire file.
- **Pretty-printed output:** selecting `nodes[]` entries by `type`, with their `summary`, `filePath` and `complexity`, is a structural query that grep cannot do reliably.
- **No extractor named:** the document names no `jq` dependency or script, while Delivery promises "no installer, manifest, or CLI change".
- **Volume:** file-level nodes for a real engagement codebase can still number in the thousands, and no budget or sampling rule is given.
- **Fields with no source in the stated schema:** the analysis doc promises "entry points" and Initial Technical Direction promises "languages, frameworks, dependencies"; neither appears in the node/edge/layer shape, and the contents of `project` are never described.
- **Initiative candidates:** "complexity clustering" is named with no algorithm or criteria.

findings.title: Graph contract is asserted from memory of v2.8.1, with no version check or drift behaviour
findings.description:
The schema is taken "from the plugin's own reference" for a plugin the document itself calls "actively developed".
- **Only one failure mode handled:** "graph missing". Nothing covers `tour[]` absent or empty, renamed fields, or a partial graph from an interrupted run.
- **Silent-degradation risk:** a concept doc built without the tour would still look complete, which conflicts with the project's no-silent-fallback rule.
- **No fixture:** no `.understand-anything/` directory exists in this repo, so there is no real graph to test against. The project's parsing rule requires a fixture in the actual production format.
- **Plugin check contradicts a principle:** Flow step 1 requires verifying the plugin is installed, yet "Graph is an input, not a dependency" and the graph is tracked in git. A teammate with the committed graph but no plugin would be blocked for no reason.
- **Detection mechanism unstated:** the document does not say how a markdown skill detects a user-scope marketplace plugin.

findings.title: Staleness check will fire on essentially every run because the graph is tracked
findings.description:
`meta.json` records the `gitCommitHash` at analysis time, and the hygiene section says `meta.json` and the graph stay tracked. Committing them moves `HEAD`, so the hash differs from `HEAD` by at least one commit immediately after a fresh analysis.
- **Warning fatigue:** a "prominent" warning that always fires stops being read, defeating the stated purpose.
- **Fix:** compare on changes outside `.understand-anything/` (and ideally within `analyzedFiles`), not on raw hash inequality.
- **Unhandled cases:** a dirty working tree (hash equals `HEAD` but the graph is stale), and a recorded hash that is unreachable after rebase, squash or shallow clone, where "commit distance" cannot be computed.
- **"Provenance" is undefined:** no frontmatter field or body section is named, and it is unclear whether it applies to the concept doc as well as the analysis doc.

findings.title: Index allocation contradicts itself and collides with other uses of the 900 band
findings.description:
- **Internal contradiction:** Output Conventions says "no change to `file-naming-conventions.md`" and then sanctions overflow past 949. Resolved Design Decisions says "in the 940-949 reserved range" with no mention of overflow.
- **Collisions:** the project conventions name 990 as the standing-fixes slice, and maintenance slices already use 908, 913 and 914. "Remaining slots in the 900 band as needed" has no stated ceiling or exclusion list.
- **Conflicting identity models for the overview:** "incrementing per run… each run is an independent sample" means every `/sq:overview` run mints a new index. The Output section instead describes one `{index}-analysis.overview.md` with a topic suffix for extras. A regenerated client document is a revision, not a sample.
- **No allocator:** nothing says who computes the next index or what happens at exhaustion. With seven slots left and per-run consumption, exhaustion is near-term.

findings.title: Capability 2's source table depends on the concept, which is absent on the "tested path"
findings.description:
Problem, Audience and Approach are sourced only from concept sections, yet Inputs calls the no-concept case "the tested path, not an edge case".
- **No fallback column:** the only fallback is "initiative plan plus interview", and no interview is designed for Capability 2.
- **Contradicts the derivation rule:** "Client document is derived, not authored" and "every claim traces to an input artifact". Interview answers are new, unapproved claims going straight into a client deliverable.
- **Weak sources for other fields:** Scope cites "non-goals" and Risks cites "initiative plan notes", neither of which the initiative plan format guarantees.
- **Status source is unreliable:** in the real plan, initiative 900 reads `not_started` while slices 908–914 have been worked on. "Status is honest" cannot be met from that field alone.
- **Invalid example:** the translation example "Initiative 140 status draft" uses `draft`, which Output Conventions says the gate rejects.

findings.title: Emphasis parameter is both specified and deferred
findings.description: Translation Rules says "Emphasis is a generation parameter". Resolved Design Decisions says "one neutral document… An emphasis parameter is added only if real use demonstrates the need". Delete the Translation Rules sentence; the Resolved Decision is the proportionate choice.

findings.title: Capability 1 output locations contradict Output Conventions, and write semantics are unspecified
findings.description:
Output Conventions says both capabilities write to `user/analysis/` with `docType: analysis`. Capability 1's main output is `project-guides/000-concept.{project}.md` with `docType: concept`, plus a possible initiative plan.
- **Existing concept:** nothing says what happens if `000-concept` already exists. Its User-Provided Concept section is one the skill must never modify.
- **Existing initiative plan:** squadron already has `001-initiative-plan.squadron.md`. "Written only on explicit confirmation" does not say whether confirmation appends, overwrites or refuses.
- **Unconfirmed candidates:** it is not stated where candidates live before confirmation (the analysis doc, or chat only).
- **User-Provided Concept contents:** putting interview answers there "verbatim" needs a rule for PM answers that are fragments or corrections across turns. Otherwise the skill is editing the one section it may not edit.

findings.title: Tracked-artifact list is incomplete and tracking a large generated graph has unexamined cost
findings.description:
- **`intermediate/scan-result.json` is unclassified:** it is neither in the ignore entry nor in the "Not ignored" list. By default it gets tracked, though it is machine-incremental state.
- **Repo cost:** the document calls the graph "large" and tracks it anyway. Churn, merge conflicts on generated JSON, and the interaction with `config.json`'s `autoUpdate` are not discussed.
- **Motivation claim unchecked:** I could not confirm that tracking `meta.json` "makes staleness visible in review" works as described; given the staleness finding above, it may show the opposite.

findings.title: Delivery section has loose ends for the first-party command
findings.description:
- **Duplicate paragraphs:** Delivery contains two "Capability (b)" paragraphs that should be merged.
- **Existing test will fail:** `tests/cli/test_install_commands.py` asserts an exact set of nine command files, so adding `overview.md` needs a test change that Delivery does not mention.
- **Possible CLI mapping:** that test also maps command files such as `review.md` and `shutdown.md` to `sq` subcommands. I did not confirm whether every file must map to one, and the document does not say whether `/sq:overview` is prompt-only. Dependencies cites [100] "CLI command registration", which implies a CLI surface.
- **Placement argument cuts both ways:** (b) is kept out of the analysis dispatcher because it "audits nothing", yet its output is `docType: analysis` in `user/analysis/`.
- **Stale name:** the initiative plan entry still calls the artifact a "brief" in one place.
- **Skill-name ambiguity:** dispatcher namespacing separates the typed commands, but a pack skill named `understand` alongside the plugin's `/understand` can still be confused when the model selects a skill by name or description.

findings.title: No verification strategy for prompt-only skills
findings.description: Cross-cutting, so no single section applies. The document calls the no-concept path "tested" and promises gate-valid frontmatter, but defines no test mechanism. At minimum, each skill should end by running `cf validate frontmatter` on what it wrote, and the slice should include a golden run against squadron's own repo.

findings.title: Scope is proportionate
findings.description: Two markdown skills, no new docType, no pipeline action, no vendoring, per-audience variants deferred. Nothing warrants cutting, and no scope from the initiative plan entry is dropped.
